name: hypertension
title: Outpatient Evaluation of Hypertension
description: Adult patient presents to primary care with newly discovered elevated blood pressure readings. Covers hypertension diagnosis, initial workup, lifestyle counseling, cardiovascular risk assessment, and medication discussion.
clinicalInvariants: Chief complaint: persistent headaches over the past two weeks, with elevated home blood pressure readings (150-160/90-98)
Conditions: pre-diabetes (HbA1c 6.0%), mild hyperlipidemia (TC 228, LDL 148), overweight (BMI 29.2)
Medications: ibuprofen PRN 2-3x/week (contributing to elevated BP), fish oil occasional
Family history: father with HTN and MI at 62, mother with HTN and T2DM, brother with HTN
Clinical findings: BP 156/94 right arm, 152/92 left arm, HR 78, no end-organ damage signs
Assessment: Stage 2 hypertension (newly diagnosed), pre-diabetes, hyperlipidemia, NSAID contribution
Management: home BP monitoring, baseline labs, lifestyle modifications (DASH diet, exercise, sodium reduction, weight loss), NSAID cessation, consider ACE/ARB if BP remains elevated
Provider questions and SP responses remain substantively identical across all variants
